title: Lichtspiel Opus 1
note: Among the first abstract animated films shown publicly. Shape and colour moving to music.

title: Rhythmus 21
note: Squares and rectangles on a black ground. Motion as pure rhythm, no subject.

title: Symphonie Diagonale
note: Line drawings that grow and shrink along a diagonal axis.

title: Rhythm in Light
note: Light, reflection and objects filmed to music. Early American abstract animation.

title: A Colour Box
note: Painted straight onto film stock. Also an advert for the GPO.

title: An Optical Poem
note: Paper shapes on wires, timed to Liszt. Made at MGM.

title: Begone Dull Care
note: Painted and scratched film cut to Oscar Peterson. Image follows sound.

title: The Man with the Golden Arm (titles)
note: White bars on black. Often cited as the start of the modern title sequence.

title: Vertigo (titles)
note: Spirals drawn with a mechanical analogue computer.

title: North by Northwest (titles)
note: Type sliding along a grid that becomes a building facade.

title: Anatomy of a Murder (titles)
note: Cut-paper body parts animated to Ellington.

title: Catalog
note: A showreel of effects from his analogue computer. Motion as a system.

title: Dr. No (titles)
note: Coloured dots and silhouettes. The template for every Bond opening.

title: Dr. Strangelove (titles)
note: Hand-drawn type laid over found footage of a B-52 refuelling.

title: Pixillation
note: Computer-generated pattern made at Bell Labs, mixed with hand animation.

title: Synchromy
note: The soundtrack shapes are also the image. You see what you hear.

title: Hunger
note: Early computer key-frame interpolation. Drawings morph into each other.

title: Arabesque
note: Harmonic motion as a design principle. Points moving at related speeds.

title: 3/78 (Objects and Transformations)
note: Sixteen points of light transforming. Minimal, strict, rule-based.

title: MTV launch identity
note: A fixed logo shape with endlessly changing surfaces. Identity as variation.

title: Se7en (titles)
note: Scratched, unstable type. Made the title sequence feel like evidence.

title: Catch Me If You Can (titles)
note: A flat graphic chase that openly borrows from Saul Bass.

title: AANAATT
note: Physical objects shot frame by frame into geometric pattern.

title: Game of Thrones (titles)
note: A clockwork map that builds itself. Information as mechanism.

title: True Detective (titles)
note: Double exposures of people and landscape.
